data.name: Puna
data.gender_notes: Puna is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Puna is derived from the Sanskrit word 'punah' meaning 'to renew, to flood'. This name is associated with freshness, renewal, and the cleansing power of water. In Hindu mythology, the god Vishnu is known to manifest in the form of a flood to cleanse the world of impurities. The name Puna carries the meaning “Flood, Deluge” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Puna usually hope their child will grow to embody flood, deluge and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Puna is a name that carries the spiritual significance of renewal and purification. It is believed to bring freshness and positivity in one's life, and to help one overcome difficulties and obstacles.
data.etymology: Puna belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Flood, Deluge.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Puna total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

In Hindu traditions, some ceremonies, especially those related to weddings and festivals, include the 'Punyahavachanam' ritual which cleanses and purifies the consciousness. This symbolizes a fresh start and the shedding of past mistakes for a better tomorrow.
data.spiritual_significance: On a deeper spiritual level, the name Puna holds the essence of the recurring cycle of life and death. It represents the belief that through transformation and renewal, an individual can rise above the imperfections and negative patterns of their past, thus reaching towards self-realization and enlightenment. The spiritual significance of Puna is a powerful reminder to let go of the old and embrace the new, fostering growth and progress along the spiritual path.

The person named Puna is seen as one who embraces change and is dedicated to the path of self-improvement.
